text:
The red rose

picked yesterday;

the fire and cinnamon

they call carnation;


the oven-baked bread

of anise and honey,

and the fish in the glass bowl

that sets it burning:


all of it yours,

little son of woman,

if only you will consent

to sleep at last.


The rose, I say;

I say the carnation.

The fruit, I say,

and I say the honey;


and the fish made of light,

and more and still more too,

if only you will sleep

until daybreak!

translation.title: If Only You Will Sleep
translation.editorial_note: The mother's escalating promises retain their nursery incantation and gently exasperated bargain.
